finding.claim: The /checkout endpoint computes the charge from client-supplied price and qty. An attacker can set any price, including 0, a negative number or a fractional value, so they pay less than the real price or get a negative charge (a refund). Negative qty also reduces the total. The server-side catalog is never consulted. The sibling /checkout-v2 handler looks prices up in the catalog and clamps qty, which shows that this handler is the unsafe one.
finding.source: req.body.items[].price and req.body.items[].qty, sent in the POST body by any authenticated user
finding.sink: req.payments.charge(req.user.id, total) at cart.js:6, which charges the attacker-computed total

trace.note: total = sum of i.price * i.qty, with both values taken directly from req.body and no validation
the unvalidated total is passed to payments.charge
the total is echoed back to the client

finding.guards_checked: There is no price lookup, no numeric or positivity check, and no qty clamp. Only one file exists in the repo, so no router-level validation middleware or mount-point checks could be inspected. The /checkout-v2 handler (lines 10-18) does have these controls, which suggests the route is a legacy one that is still reachable.

verdict.reason: cart.js:5 sums client-supplied i.price * i.qty from req.body with no catalog lookup, type, positivity or qty check, and cart.js:6 passes that total to payments.charge, while the sibling cart.js:13-14 looks up prices and clamps qty; the only attacker requirement is an authenticated user (req.user.id), and no guards exist in the file (middleware outside it can't be inspected, but nothing in the repo blocks it).
